title: "Getting Started with RDesk"
format: html

This guide walks you through building, running, and understanding your first RDesk desktop application.

## Prerequisites

RDesk requires:

* **Operating System**: Windows 10 or Windows 11 (64-bit).
* **R Environment**: R >= 4.0.0 (R 4.5 recommended).
* **WebView2 Runtime**: Pre-installed on Windows 11 and modern Windows 10 updates (Evergreen WebView2).

## Installation

Install RDesk from GitHub:

```r
# Install development version
remotes::install_github("Janakiraman-311/RDesk@release/v1.0.7-windows")
```

## Creating Your First Application

The easiest way to start is with `rdesk_create_app()`, which scaffolds a complete application structure:

```r
library(RDesk)

# Create a dark-themed analytics dashboard
rdesk_create_app("MyDashboard", theme = "dark")
```

### Application Structure

Your generated application contains the following modular hierarchy:

```
MyDashboard/
├── app.R              # Main application entry point and window launcher
├── DESCRIPTION        # Application metadata and R package dependencies
├── R/                 # Modular backend R logic
│   ├── data.R         # Data loading and preprocessing
│   ├── plots.R        # Chart generation (ggplot2 -> base64 PNG)
│   └── server.R       # Event handlers and IPC message routers
└── www/               # Frontend user interface assets
    ├── index.html     # HTML5 dashboard layout
    ├── css/
    │   └── style.css  # Application styles (theme presets)
    └── js/
        ├── app.js     # Frontend event listeners and UI updater
        └── rdesk.js   # RDesk JavaScript bridge library
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Separation of Concerns
Notice how data loading, visualization, and event handling are separated into distinct source files inside `R/`. When `app.R` starts, it automatically sources all files in `R/` into the application environment.
:::

## Anatomy of `app.R`

Here is what the core application entry point looks like:

```r
# app.R
library(RDesk)
library(ggplot2)

app_dir <- getwd()

# Source all modular logic from R/
invisible(lapply(
  sort(list.files("R", pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE)),
  source
))

# Create native window instance
app <- App$new(
  title  = "My Dashboard",
  width  = 1100L,
  height = 740L,
  www    = file.path(app_dir, "www")
)

# Register message handlers from R/server.R
init_handlers(app)

# Start event loop
app$run()
```

## Handling Events & IPC

Communication between your web UI and R happens via JSON message envelopes.

### 1. In JavaScript (`www/js/app.js`)

When a user clicks a button or changes a filter, send a message to R:

```javascript
// Request data from R
rdesk.send("get_data", { filter: "all" });

// Listen for response from R
rdesk.on("data_ready", function(payload) {
  console.log("Received rows:", payload.rows.length);
  document.getElementById("main-chart").src = payload.chart;
});
```

### 2. In R (`R/server.R`)

Register handlers on your `app` object using `app$on_message()`:

```r
init_handlers <- function(app) {
  # Handler for "get_data" requests
  app$on_message("get_data", function(payload) {
    df <- load_my_data(payload$filter)
    
    # Return list which auto-serializes to JSON
    list(
      rows  = rdesk_df_to_list(df)$rows,
      chart = make_chart(df),
      kpis  = list(count = nrow(df))
    )
  })
}
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Automatic JSON Serialization
Return values from `app$on_message()` handlers are automatically serialized to JSON and sent back to the JavaScript frontend with the corresponding response event name (e.g. `get_data_result`).
:::

## Packaging for Distribution

To bundle your application into a standalone desktop distribution that runs on machines without R:

```r
RDesk::build_app(
  app_dir  = "MyDashboard",
  app_name = "MyDashboard",
  version  = "1.0.0",
  out_dir  = "dist"
)
```

The output in `dist/` is a complete `.zip` distribution containing:

* `MyDashboard.exe`: Compiled launcher stub.
* `runtime/`: Complete, self-contained R runtime.
* `packages/`: All required packages and their dependency closures.
* `app/`: Your application code and UI assets.
